intro: Convert liters to milliliters (L to mL) instantly for cooking recipes, beverage bottling, aquarium dosing, and laboratory measurements. Under the SI metric system, 1 liter (or litre) equals exactly 1,000 milliliters—simply multiply liters by 1,000, or shift the decimal point three places to the right. Use this ltr to mL calculator above or browse common metric capacities from 0.1 L to 1,000 L below.
alsoWrittenAs: L to mL, ltr to mL, litres to millilitres, liter to milliliter, L to cc

mistakesAndEdgeCases.title: 750 mL Bottle vs. 750 L Tank & Lab Concentration Scaling
items: Watch direction on common bottle sizes: a standard wine bottle is 750 mL (0.75 L), whereas 750 L is a 750,000 mL storage tank. To convert milliliters back into liters, tap Swap or open our Milliliters to Liters converter.

For laboratory mass-concentration units (per liter vs. per milliliter), the denominator scales by 1,000× while the numerator prefix may also change: 1 µg/L (1 mcg/L) equals 1 ng/mL, 1 ng/L equals 1 pg/mL, and 1 ng/L equals 0.001 ng/mL.

faqs.question: How many milliliters are in 1 liter?
faqs.answer: There are exactly 1,000 milliliters (mL) in 1 liter (L). Conversely, 1 milliliter equals 0.001 liters.

faqs.question: How do I convert liters to milliliters?
faqs.answer: Multiply liters by 1,000 (mL = L × 1,000), or shift the decimal point three places to the right. For example, 45.23 L equals 45,230 mL.

faqs.question: What is 750 liters in milliliters compared to a 750 mL bottle?
faqs.answer: 750 liters equals 750,000 mL. In the opposite direction, a standard 750 mL wine bottle equals 0.75 liters (750 ÷ 1,000).

faqs.question: Is 1 liter equal to 1,000 cc?
faqs.answer: Yes. Because 1 milliliter equals exactly 1 cubic centimeter (1 cc), 1 liter equals both 1,000 mL and 1,000 cc.
